guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / pelvic fractures and major trauma
title: Pelvic fracture after cycling collision
setting: Road cycling event. Cyclist hit by a car, thrown from bike, lying on road. Severe pelvic and thigh pain, loss of sensation in feet, pale, clammy.
verdictExplanation: Suspected pelvic fracture with life-threatening internal bleeding, loss of sensation, and severe shock (pulse 110 bpm, BP 90/60). Sick: immediate immobilization and 999.

shared.danger: Car involved in collision, other vehicles on road
shared.response: Responsive but in severe pain, becoming unresponsive
shared.circulation: Weak, irregular pulse, pale skin, suspect internal pelvic bleeding

er.disability: Confused, loss of sensation in feet
er.exposure: Recent physical exertion, outdoors on asphalt road

history.complaint: Severe pelvic and left thigh pain
history.history: Collision with a moving car while cycling 10 minutes ago, thrown from bicycle, helmet thrown off
history.injuries: Suspect pelvic fracture, bruising and swelling around pelvis and left thigh

followUp.question: What is the priority first aid intervention for a suspected pelvic fracture?

options.text: Call 999, keep the patient completely still, do not move the legs, apply a pelvic binder if ER trained, and treat for shock
Encourage the patient to sit up and bend his knees to check mobility
Log-roll the patient onto his side to inspect his back immediately
Force him to stand and walk to the roadside to clear traffic

followUp.explanation: Pelvic fractures can cause massive, life-threatening internal bleeding. Call 999 immediately. Keep the patient completely still, do not move the legs. If ER trained, apply a pelvic binder. Never roll the patient or allow sitting/standing as it can cause catastrophic bleeding.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Call 999 immediately. Keep him completely still, reassure, keep warm.
levelFlags.erNotes: Suspected pelvic fracture with hypovolemic shock. Apply pelvic binder (if trained). Administer high-flow oxygen, check BGL, monitor vitals, and arrange rapid transport.
